newsitem.title: USA: U.S. demand for foreign light crudes on rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. demand for foreign light crudes on rise.

text.p: U.S. refiner demand for light, sweet crudes was underscored by the fixing of another million barrels of Brent crude early November for the U.S. Gulf.
Traders said the arbitrage was weak, but refiners wanting the barrels would still pay the premiums for it.
The barrels on the vessel were believed earlier sold to a U.S. Gulf refiners closer to West Texas Intermediate parity, than the present level around WTI plus 15-20 cents cif.
"It's a mystery how these traders are making money with the arb as narrow as it is," an East Coast trader said, noting although a modest improvement in the Nov WTI/Brent spread.
The spread expanded to $1.10 a barrel, up 15 cents from Wednesday, helped by the rally in WTI.
A trader with a collection of Brent cargoes in hand was also thought looking for opportunities to sell into the U.S.
Within the region, Latin American supplies were ample and seen offered into both the West and Gulf coasts.
Oriente for second-half Oct was valued around WTI minus $2.00 cif to the Gulf Coast, with West Coast prices seen at Alaska North Slope minus $1.00.
Cusiana premiums firmed on good demand, asked at Dec +15 cts for late Oct.
Elsewhere, premiums for light crudes were also buoyant with distillate-rich Oseberg reported traded in late U.S. markets at Dated Brent plus 48 cents fob for Oct 25-27.
A prompt cargo of Palanca for Oct 15-17 was also done at Dated Brent +26 cts.
In the U.S. after market, paper dealings were thinned by volatility in outright levels.
A partial cargo of Dec Brent traded at $23.25 a barrel, seven cents firmer than London's IPE close. Intermonth Brent moved for Nov/Dec at 51 cents, within the earlier London cash session range.
